clue.text: Remorseful as editor consumes ham sandwich

indicators.note: whatever consumes something takes it inside itself, so one piece swallows another
a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so outer letters surround inner ones

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor feels guilty after wolfing down a ham sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: AS and ED join as the bread, with HAM as the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed means feeling guilt and regret over something done, which is what remorse is.

clue.text: Mix right up — put one's foot in it!

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the noun: the thing one puts a foot in

parts.note: to mix something is to stir it
R is the usual abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirs things up and then commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot in it' looks like the idiom for making a gaffe; read literally it describes a rider's foot-rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop hanging from a saddle into which a horse rider places a foot.

clue.text: A profit repeated

definitions.note: adjective in the clue, adverb for the answer: it happened again

parts.note: taken as written
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: A company records the same profit a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done again is done once more, a further time, which is what repetition involves.

clue.text: Go and sit back; I'm up and around. Yes, me, me, me!

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it on both sides
going back means running the letters from right to left

parts.note: the speaker saying I'm refers to themself, me
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit back and relax insists on being the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old Quiptic clue: I'm stands for ME, which turned up becomes EM and wraps round GO plus the reversed SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive self-importance, and the repeated 'me' mimics someone talking only about themselves.

clue.text: Russian companies get plunder

parts.note: COS is the abbreviation for companies
to sack a town is to plunder it

explanation.surface: Russian firms help themselves to loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were a people of southern Russia and Ukraine, famed as horsemen, so a Cossack is a Russian.

clue.text: Speaker in search of good political theme for a Tory

parts.note: surface padding describing what a speechmaker looks for

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in, inside, the run of words that ends the clue

parts.note: spans the end of 'for', all of 'a' and the start of 'Tory'

explanation.surface: A politician hunts for a good theme for a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'search of good political theme' is surface padding describing what a speechmaker does.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is someone who gives formal public speeches, so a speaker in the rhetorical sense.

clue.text: Fellow at the entrance, we hear, is a docker

parts.note: a man's name standing for any fellow

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: the entrance to a house is its door

explanation.surface: A man standing at a doorway turns out to work on the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a labourer who loads and unloads ships in port, the same job as a docker.

clue.text: Warning for an amusing person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: advice to take care
second meaning: an old-fashioned word for a comical or surprising character

explanation.surface: Someone is warned off because they are a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: Caution is an alert to danger, and colloquially 'a caution' is a person who makes others laugh.

clue.text: Quote the rhymes of Edward Lear? Rubbish!

parts.note: to quote words is to utter them
Lear's collections are titled A Book of Nonsense and Nonsense Songs

explanation.surface: Someone recites Lear's verses and is dismissed as talking twaddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the Victorian author of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter nonsense is complete drivel, an exclamation dismissing something as worthless talk.

clue.text: Last eiderdown taken off bed for singer

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter comes away

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the following word only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone strips the duvet off a bed for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Causing affront? Such an act has nothing on us!

parts.note: an act that causes affront is an outrage
O is zero, nothing
taken as written, placed on the end

explanation.surface: An offensive performance that no one in the audience can match.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrageous behaviour is shockingly offensive and causes widespread affront.

clue.text: Could be in Ur, perhaps, or in Borneo

definitions.note: describes the place rather than naming it: a country in Borneo

indicators.note: 'could be' asks what these letters might become if rearranged
perhaps signals one possible reworking of the letters

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a site might be in ancient Ur or out in Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the northern coast of the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Obscure man goes round twiddling toes

indicators.note: going round sends the front of the string to the back, like a wheel turning
twiddling is fiddling about with something, so the letters get moved around

parts.note: any man's name will do
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd fellow paces about while wiggling his toes.
explanation.walkthrough: ERIC followed by the rearranged toes, then rotated so the man moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small specialist group, so it is obscure to most.

clue.text: Plant to attack with an assagai?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: meant for spearing, since an assagai is a spear

explanation.walkthrough: An assagai is a light southern African spear; the question mark flags the pun splitting the word into spear and mint, said like meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common garden mint grown for flavouring, a herb and therefore a plant.

clue.text: Concerning the act that changed course

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the clue; the answer is the noun for such a change

parts.note: about means concerning
a turn is an act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A report on the stage performance that made a show take a new direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a complete reversal of direction or policy, a sharp change of course.

clue.text: Unsophisticated as bad feet, perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: covered in corns, as sore feet may be

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the word literally: full of corns, the hard painful skin patches on feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Corny humour is stale and naive, lacking polish, which is what unsophisticated means.

clue.text: Bend down at the entrance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lower the head and shoulders

definitions.note: describes where a stoop is rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a raised porch or steps outside a front door, chiefly American

explanation.surface: Someone ducks their head as they go through a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to lean forward and lower oneself; a stoop is also the porch steps of a house.

clue.text: Stress from having 10 offspring round one

parts.note: the number written as a word

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a son is one's offspring
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A parent of ten children is under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental strain or nervous pressure, the same state as stress.

clue.text: Exhausted skill with wild deer

parts.note: a knack is a skill

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter worn out from tackling untamed deer.
explanation.walkthrough: Knackered is everyday British slang for utterly tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knackered is to be completely worn out, tired to the point of collapse.

clue.text: Annoyance because tea served with a smile

parts.note: cha is informal British for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Irritation at being handed a cuppa by a grinning waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is distress or vexation at a failure or humiliation, a form of annoyance.

clue.text: What Gray did in a churchyard?

definitions.text: What Gray did in a churchyard?

parts.words: What Gray did in a churchyard?
parts.note: surface reading: an anecdote about someone visiting a graveyard
setter's reading: Thomas Gray, the poet of the famous lament written in a country churchyard

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard (1751); the answer is the verb for composing such a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To elegise is to write a mournful poem lamenting the dead, which is exactly what the poem does.

clue.text: Dagger mark becoming so blue

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters change form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A printed dagger symbol turning a sad blue colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is a printer's reference symbol shaped like a dagger, used to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Take horse out of shelter that's shaky

definitions.meaning: first meaning, punning: to remove from a stable, read as un- plus stable

explanation.surface: Leading a horse out of a rickety barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense invents a verb by reading the word as un-stable, undoing the stabling of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstable is liable to wobble or collapse, lacking firmness, as a shaky thing does.

clue.text: Given inspiration in time and entertained

indicators.note: something given into another's hands is received and held inside
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks time in years
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: An artist struck by inspiration just in time, and enjoying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be entertained or diverted, finding something enjoyable or funny.

clue.text: Remove one's headgear — a United Nations beret?

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for United Nations
a beret is a kind of cap

explanation.surface: A peacekeeper takes off the famous blue beret.
explanation.walkthrough: UN peacekeepers wear blue berets, so the wordplay also illustrates the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap is to take off one's hat or cap, typically as a mark of respect.

clue.text: One who sees USA is viler somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged freely

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An observer judges America to be the more wicked place.
explanation.definitionFit: A visualiser forms mental pictures, seeing things in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Fastener is a hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device that grips things together

explanation.surface: A new fastening gadget proves a commercial success.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip holds sheets together, and a clip is also a quick smack with the hand.

clue.text: A single head in its entirety

parts.note: a single thing is one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Describes a lone skull kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is the state of being unified and whole, complete in its entirety.

clue.text: Fish photographer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sea fish with sharp teeth
second meaning: informal for someone taking pictures, especially a press photographer

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests a photographer of fish; in fact the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Red snapper is an edible fish, and a snapper is slang for someone who snaps photos.
